sources.why: Graduate visa overview: eligibility, how long you can stay (2 years / 18 months / 3 years PhD), cannot extend, switching example to Skilled Worker, work rights.
Graduate visa application fee and healthcare surcharge amounts; linked from the overview cost section.
Documents for a Graduate visa application (passport, CAS, BRP). Linked from the Graduate guide contents.
Skilled Worker overview: approved employer, certificate of sponsorship, eligible occupation, salary, duration up to 5 years, ILR mention, apply timing relative to CoS start date.
Job eligibility: occupation codes (CASCOT), salary framework, approved employers/sponsors, CoS as an electronic record with a reference number, link to the sponsor licence fees.
When a lower salary than the usual rate can apply (immigration salary list, new entrant/recent graduate, PhD). Linked from 'your job'.
Switching to Skilled Worker from inside the UK, including from a Graduate visa; who cannot switch; apply-before-current-visa-expires.
Skilled Worker fees, healthcare surcharge, and money-to-support-yourself / sponsor-can-support-you rules.
English language requirement and exemptions; needed for 'what you must show' questions.
Extending Skilled Worker (contrast with Graduate: Graduate cannot be extended). Includes transition rules for occupation skill level.
Documents for a Skilled Worker application, including CoS reference number, occupation code, sponsor licence number. Linked from overview and your-job.

What a sponsor licence is; sponsoring someone does not guarantee they get a visa; CoS after licence. Context for licence-vs-sponsorship questions. The licensed-sponsor register itself is a large download/changelog and is not ingested.
